messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: calculating pooling factors
parts:
Hi!

I am running a random intercept + slope linear model and I am interested in calculating the pooling factors (http://dx.doi.org/10.1198/004017005000000517) for each random effect. Is there a direct way to get this with rstanarm?

I (think) get what I want, but rstanarm usually has very clever and elegant ways to get things and I wonder if I missed some feature.

This would make a great addition to the vignettes on partial pooling as it puts down a number on how much actual borrowing is going on for a given factor, nicely illustrating the point of the hierarchical model as I find.

Thanks.

Sebastian

Here is my schematic R code (Bfit contains the stanreg object):

rowVars <- function(x) apply(x, 1, var)

## for year==0 => intercept only (abase_fit has year=0 which is the linear predictor)
post_base_full <- posterior_linpred(Bfit, newdata=abase_fit)
post_base_pop <- posterior_linpred(Bfit, newdata=abase_fit, re.form=~0)

## individual deviations
post_base_eps <- post_base_full - post_base_pop

Epost_base_eps <- colMeans(post_base_eps)
Vpost_base_eps <- rowVars(post_base_eps)

pool_inter <- 1 - var(Epost_base_eps) / mean(Vpost_base_eps)

pool_inter

Then I repeat things with year=1 and subtract the intercept...
